docs/releases/v0.5.0.md:46:These fields remain additive. Existing Gotify clients may ignore Gotify MU-specific collaboration data and continue normal notification reception.
docs/releases/v0.5.0.md:175:The Docker Compose deployment binds SMTP and Syslog receiver ports to loopback by default. Administrators must deliberately set `GOTIFY_MU_RECEIVER_BIND` to a trusted host/LAN address when remote devices need access.
docs/releases/v0.5.0.md:192:Native Go plugins execute in the Gotify MU server process and therefore remain trusted extensions rather than sandboxed code. Only install plugins from trusted publishers.

docs/releases/v1.0.2.md:5:# Gotify MU v1.0.2
docs/releases/v1.0.2.md:7:Gotify MU 1.0.2 simplifies managed updates and returns Docker deployment to one persistent Gotify MU container.
docs/releases/v1.0.2.md:13:1. Gotify MU checks GitHub for the latest published release.
docs/releases/v1.0.2.md:16:4. Gotify MU restarts into the new version and the browser reloads.
docs/releases/v1.0.2.md:22:Docker Compose now defines only the `gotify-mu` service.
docs/releases/v1.0.2.md:24:There is no persistent `gotify-mu-updater` service and no updater shared token. The main container has controlled access to the Docker socket for managed self-updates. When an update is requested, it launches a short-lived `gotify-mu-update-worker` container from the currently installed Gotify MU image. That worker exists only for the update operation, preserves the current runtime configuration and persistent data mount, verifies the replacement container, performs automatic rollback when necessary, and removes itself when finished.

These include legacy request headers/routes/config names, legacy on-disk migration paths, the upstream `github.com/gotify/plugin-api` and `github.com/gotify/location` dependencies, required plugin ABI entrypoint names, license attribution, and historical release notes.
